# Paper figures (generated by `tests/make_paper_figures.py`; do not edit by hand)

One row per figure. Every number in a caption is read from the source CSV by the script. Markers: **filled** = Holm-significant median, **hollow** = not significant, **plus** = not tested; every run is a point. Figures with n = 3 are descriptive (bars, no test). Widths: 3.5 in (single column) or 7.16 in (double column).

| figure | file (PDF and PNG in `paper/figures/`) | script function | source CSV(s) | n per cell | draft caption (at most 3 sentences) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F-E4: Wall-clock by arm vs C0 (E4 F1, F4) | `fig_e4_wallclock_by_arm` | `fig_e4` | results/analysis/gate_e/e4/e4_runs.csv<br>results/analysis/gate_e/e4/primary_comparisons.csv | 10 runs per arm, including C0 | RTX 5070 Ti, driver 595.91.07, stock prefetcher on: wall-clock change of the staging arms relative to the median of C0 (the shipped driver) on Stencil-24K and GraphBFS-23 (E4 family F1), and of perfect off-path staging with the in-path prefetcher off, C6-W512 (family F4, right). Each run is a point; markers are medians, filled when Holm-significant (two-sided Mann-Whitney U, n = 10 per arm). At W = 512 the Stencil-24K arm is -4.93% against C0, while C6-W512 is +191.95%. |
| F-E5: D(t) and wall-clock vs threshold (E5) | `fig_e5_threshold_dose_response` | `fig_e5` | results/analysis/gate_e/e5/e5_runs.csv<br>results/analysis/gate_e/e5/fault_reduction.csv<br>results/analysis/gate_e/e5/wallclock_comparisons.csv | 10 runs per cell | RTX 5070 Ti, stock prefetcher, Stencil-24K: D(t) = 1 - (median demand faults of C7W512) / (median of C0 at the same threshold) and the wall-clock change of C7W512 against C0 at the same threshold. Each run is a point; markers are medians, filled when Holm-significant (two-sided Mann-Whitney U, n = 10 per cell). D is +0.4009 at the shipped threshold 51, +0.5337 at 75 and -0.0215 with the rule disabled (100). |
| F-E6: C0 and C7W512 vs threshold 0-51 (E6) | `fig_e6_threshold_baseline` | `fig_e6` | results/analysis/gate_e/e6/e6_runs.csv<br>results/analysis/gate_e/e6/secondary_wall.csv<br>results/analysis/gate_e/e6/secondary_demand.csv<br>results/analysis/gate_e/e6/family1_primary.csv | 10 runs per cell | RTX 5070 Ti, E3a-2 module, Stencil-24K, prefetcher on: process wall-clock and demand faults of C0 (speculation off) and C7W512 (oracle, W = 512) at each prefetch threshold. Each run is a point; markers are medians, filled when the within-threshold comparison is Holm-significant (two-sided Mann-Whitney U, n = 10 per cell), hollow when not, a plus when the cell was not tested. The C0 median is 1.0262 s at threshold 0 against 1.1298 s at the shipped 51, and C7W512 at 51 is 1.0918 s. |
| F-E7: Threshold effect per workload, two platforms (E7, E7-T4) | `fig_e7_threshold_by_workload_two_platforms` | `fig_e7` | results/analysis/gate_e/e7/e7_runs.csv<br>results/analysis/gate_e/e7/family_a.csv<br>results/analysis/gate_e/e7/family_b.csv<br>results/analysis/t4/e7t4_runs.csv<br>results/analysis/t4/family_a.csv<br>results/analysis/t4/family_b.csv | 10 runs per cell on each platform (separate analyses, never pooled) | Stock driver 595.91.07, prefetcher on, no speculation: wall-clock change of threshold 0 and 25 against the shipped threshold 51 (each cell's own median), per workload, on the RTX 5070 Ti (left) and the Tesla T4 (right); the two platforms are analysed separately and not pooled. Each run is a point; markers are medians, filled when Holm-significant (two-sided Mann-Whitney U, n = 10 per cell; Stencil-24K shows threshold 0 only, from family A). The oversubscribed Stencil cell was not run on the T4. On Stencil-24K the change at threshold 0 is -9.57% on the RTX 5070 Ti and -5.07% on the T4, and 12 of 14 T4 family-B tests are significantly faster, 6 of them (GraphBFS-23, SGEMM, Stencil-8K and cuFFT) by less than the achieved-n minimum detectable effect (white x). |
| F-E8: Threshold effect vs sparsity (E8) | `fig_e8_sparse_access` | `fig_e8` | results/analysis/gate_e/e8/e8_runs.csv<br>results/analysis/gate_e/e8/primary_tests.csv | 10 runs per cell | RTX 5070 Ti, stock driver, synthetic sparse-access benchmark: wall-clock change of threshold 0 and 25 against threshold 51 as the number of pages touched per 2 MB block grows, with the array in memory (left) and 1.5x oversubscribed (right). Each run is a point; markers are medians, filled when Holm-significant (two-sided Mann-Whitney U, one Holm family of 16 tests, n = 10 per cell). With one page per block the change at threshold 0 is +3.95% in memory and +84.96% oversubscribed. |
| F-E9: Migrated bytes (E9) | `fig_e9_migrated_bytes` | `fig_e9` | results/analysis/gate_e/e9/e9_runs.csv<br>results/analysis/gate_e/e9/cell_medians.csv | 3 runs per cell (descriptive; no tests) | RTX 5070 Ti, stock driver, nsys-traced runs: unified-memory bytes migrated host to device and device to host per run at threshold 0 and at the shipped 51, for the sparse-access benchmark (oversubscribed and in memory) and Stencil-24K. Bars are medians of 3 traced runs, points are the runs, and the axis is symmetric-logarithmic; no statistical test is applied (counts are under tracing). With one page per block on the oversubscribed array, threshold 0 migrates 129.8 GiB in and 114.6 GiB out, against 4.0 and 3.5 GiB at 51. |
| F-PH: Per-phase medians, Stencil-24K C1 vs C6-L4096 (E1 Part B) | `fig_ph_phase_medians` | `fig_ph` | results/analysis/gate_e/e1/partb_phase_totals.csv | 3 runs (C1) and 3 runs (C6-L4096) | RTX 5070 Ti, Stencil-24K, prefetcher off, E1 Part B: median time per run spent in each phase of the fault-dispatch window (D4 is the address-space lock hold and contains D5). Bars are medians, points are the runs; no statistical test is applied (n = 3 and 3). D5 is 1.595 s with C1 and 0.914 s with the oracle (C6, L = 4096). |
